shared_elements: stone surface worked in low relief
anthropomorphic form (standing figure in B; figural monolith in A)
horizontal incised bands or lines crossing the surface
weathered, pitted stone with surface loss
justification: Both are weathered stone surfaces carved in shallow relief and each carries a distinct circular disc/roundel and horizontal banding, which is about as far as the correspondence goes. The decisive difference is that A is a three-dimensional freestanding block whose ornament wraps a schematic, blocky body in coarse incised abstraction, while B is a flat panel with a naturalistically modelled animal and attendant set within a framed register above a repeating rosette border.
